text:
Asha: Heads-up — I'm prototyping a tiny loader shim to stream legacy safetensors (v0) from S3 but keep using our shard-hotspot warmup heuristics. Sketch below, want quick feedback before I open an RFC.
Sam: Streaming v0 sounds useful. Biggest question: how do we validate partial streams? Per-chunk checksums or rely on a manifest?
Luca: Per-chunk checksums + header probe seems safest. Extra HEAD calls, but we avoid full download and can detect corrupt ranges early. :+1:

Asha: Agree. Proposal: each shard file exposes a short "chunk index" at the start (backported by shim) with N checksums. Loader does small ranged GET for header, then requests chunks lazily. If a ranged GET fails or checksum mismatch -> fall back to full mmap/multipart GET. Fast failure path.
Asha: Example config I sketched:
```
loader:
  mode: streaming
  ranged_probe_size: 16KB
  chunk_size: 4MB
  fallback_ms: 120
  fallback_mode: mmap
  hotspot_first: true
  checksum_cache_path: /var/cache/weights-checksums
```

Sam: Two tradeoffs: 1) HEAD/ranged probes add latency on cold starts (but small). 2) Storing per-chunk checksums increases bundle size slightly. Both okay if we get a big drop in cold-start token latency for long prefixes.

Nora: We need telemetry before we decide defaults: histogram of prefix lengths, per-shard first-byte latency, ranged GET error rate, and checksum mismatch counts. Also surface when fallback triggers (hot vs cold).

infra-bot: CI:nightly - weights-staging job scheduled to run the streaming loader e2e on cluster "weights-staging" tonight at 02:00 UTC (job id: ws-2026-041). Logs will post to #eng-ml after run.

Luca: Implementation note: keep shim minimal — do not reserialize safetensors. Only synthesize a tiny sidecar header (JSON) with checksums and chunk metadata. That keeps backwards compatibility with other tools.

Sam: Another runtime angle: if a shard is marked "hotspot" in the model manifest, prefetch its first 2 chunks aggressively during warmup; otherwise on-demand. Saves memory and respects batching.

Asha: Perf guardrails: if ranged_probe_time > fallback_ms (120ms) OR first-chunk fetch fails > 2 attempts, switch to fallback mode for that request and emit a metric. We can tune fallback_ms after nightly run.

Nora: Also add a debug flag to force fallback so infra can test the mmap path without reuploading bundles.

Asha: OK — action items: (1) I'll push a tiny prototype PR with the header-synthesis shim and config above. (2) Nora, can you add the telemetry metrics list to the infra dashboard? (3) Luca, can you draft the sidecar header format (2 fields: chunk_checksums, chunk_byte_offsets)?

Sam: Sounds good. If nightly shows high ranged GET error rate we can add a small CDN-prefetch step for first-chunk ranges.

Asha: Thanks all — will ping when PR is up. :rocket:
